delta_constraint.description: #321 P2 item 3: the third union term of the stated budget -- the level at which constraint models exclude candidates (Bonferroni over the modelled constraints). Present exactly when a declared constraint has a violating side and no when-guard; defaults to delta_screen.

terminal_robustness.description: #321 P3 item 2 (A5): the registered robust terminal family. floor = the smallest replicate count at which the exact sign-flip bound exists at the per-look, per-challenger level (level_for_floor); skew_alpha = the studentized-third-moment pretest level. Both vetoes; absent in policies compiled before P3, which keep the t family alone.

delta_feasibility.description: #321 P3 item 3: the union term for distributional constraints (semantics mean | chance:<alpha>), present exactly when one is declared; defaults to delta_terminal. Confirm spends it over finalists x constraints x looks.

heteroscedasticity.description: #321 P3 item 1: the registered Brown-Forsythe check of M3 at confirm (single-objective). A veto on the model half, so it spends no delta; absent in policies compiled before P3, which then skip it.

campaign_delta.description: #321 item 7: the charged cross-epoch mode (optimization.policy.campaign_delta). epoch_share is this epoch's share of the campaign-wide total (geometric: total/2^e; or a declared schedule); the epoch's delta_screen/delta_terminal(/delta_constraint) are that share split in the declared proportions (declared_split). exhausted: no share remains, so this epoch certifies nothing.

objectives.description: Multi-objective campaigns only: every objective with its own indifference width. metric/direction above are the FIRST objective's.

planner.description: WP-D (#320): optional planning-tool configuration compiled from optimization.planner and hashed with the policy. It proposes candidates only (allocate.py pool, plan-next bo_block); it is never used for inference or certification.

run_order.description: Run-order concealment (#321): derivation 2 draws every iteration's run-order seed from sha256(policy hash, iteration); the policy hash covers this random salt, recorded at compile in run_order.epoch-<e>.json. Absent = derivation 1 (the seed is the iteration index).
